The School at ICP runs open-enrolment photography courses and workshops for all skill levels.

how: Greenwich House Pottery teaches handbuilding to all levels at its Jones Street and Chelsea studios.
Greenwich House Pottery offers wheel-throwing classes for first-timers upward; Pottery NYC also runs wheel courses.
Craftsman Ave in Industry City runs tufting wall-art and rug classes using a tufting gun; other studios list punch-needle and tufting workshops.
UrbanGlass in Fort Greene offers stained glass suncatcher, projects and sampler classes.
CourseHorse lists multiple weaving classes in NYC, including Saori weaving, though the operating studio was not confirmed.
Craftsman Ave teaches beginner woodworking, including a two-day side-table build, in a professional shop.
NYC Resistor in downtown Brooklyn is a long-running member hackerspace with workshops such as KiCad PCB design; Hack Manhattan holds open houses on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Marshall Chess Club in Greenwich Village offers adult classes, instruction and tournaments; casual chess also runs in Washington Square Park.
Honors Bridge Club in Manhattan is a long-established duplicate bridge club (founded 1993).
Barcade operates classic-arcade bars in Chelsea, FiDi, St. Marks Place and Brooklyn.
Twenty Sided Store hosts weekly beginner-friendly D&D sessions with materials provided.

New mahjong social clubs and pop-up game nights have multiplied across the city.
Brooklyn Bowl is a bowling alley and music venue with lane rentals and a restaurant.
Brooklyn Brew Shop sells beer-making kits and mixes and hard-cider kits for apartment homebrewing.
Brooklyn Brew Shop sells kombucha kits, fermented hot sauce kits and fermentation supplies for home use.
The New York Hall of Science in Queens is a hands-on science museum.
Japan Society's Language Center teaches Japanese across 13 levels in 10- and 5-week sessions.
Instituto Cervantes New York runs Spanish courses in person and online.
Municipal Art Society runs guided historic and architectural walking tours of neighbourhoods such as SoHo, Grand Central and Bed-Stuy.
The Russian & Turkish Baths in the East Village have a redwood sauna, Russian and Turkish rooms.
